# ToggleSwitch

Header: `winui/ui/input/ToggleSwitch.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/input/ToggleSwitch.hpp`.

A boolean on/off switch: a pill-shaped track with a sliding thumb, an optional header above it and a label beside it that follows the state.

Use it for a setting that takes effect immediately (a [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox) is for a choice confirmed later). A click released over the control, or Space on key-up while focused, flips [checked()](#checked) and fires [on_checked_changed()](#on_checked_changed). The control reserves the width of the wider of its two labels, so flipping it never reflows its row. With animations running, the thumb slides and grows on hover. Otherwise it snaps.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> wifi{true};

auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* sw    = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ToggleSwitchControl>(true));
sw->set_header("Wi-Fi");
sw->on_checked_changed([&](bool on) { wifi = on; });

// Or declaratively, kept in step with the Property:
stack->add(ui::ToggleSwitch{
    .header             = "Airplane mode",
    .checked            = ui::bind(wifi, [](bool w) { return !w; }),
    .checked_text       = "Flying",
    .unchecked_text     = "Grounded",
    .on_checked_changed = [&](bool on) { wifi = !on; },
}.build());
window.set_content(std::move(stack));
```

## `ui::ToggleSwitch`

A boolean on/off switch, with a header above it and a label beside it that follows the state. Builds a [ui::ToggleSwitchControl](#uitoggleswitchcontrol).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> wifi{true};

window.set_content(ui::ToggleSwitch{
    .header            = "Wi-Fi",
    .checked           = wifi,
    .checked_text      = "Connected",
    .unchecked_text    = "Off",
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::ToggleSwitch{
    .header, .checked, .checked_text, .unchecked_text, .checked_icon, .unchecked_icon, .style,
    .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility,
    .on_checked_changed, .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus,
    .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-header"></span>`header` | `ui::Binding<std::string>` |  | The label above the control. Empty draws none. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-checked"></span>`checked` | `ui::TwoWayField<bool>` | `{false}` | On or off. Seeding it raises no [`.on_checked_changed`](#uitoggleswitch-on_checked_changed). |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-checked_text"></span>`checked_text` | `ui::Binding<std::optional<std::string>>` |  | The label beside the track while on; unset uses [strings()](../core/namespace-ui.md#strings).toggle_switch.on ("On"). The same text in both [`checked_text`](#uitoggleswitch-checked_text) and [`unchecked_text`](#uitoggleswitch-unchecked_text) makes a label that does not change with the state. Both empty shows no label. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-unchecked_text"></span>`unchecked_text` | `ui::Binding<std::optional<std::string>>` |  | The label while off; unset uses [strings()](../core/namespace-ui.md#strings).toggle_switch.off ("Off"). |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-checked_icon"></span>`checked_icon` | `ui::Binding<ui::IconSource>` |  | An icon in place of the on state's text, which then only names that state for UI Automation. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-unchecked_icon"></span>`unchecked_icon` | `ui::Binding<ui::IconSource>` |  | The off state's icon, as [`checked_icon`](#uitoggleswitch-checked_icon). |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_checked_changed"></span>`on_checked_changed` | `ui::Callback<void(bool)>` |  | The new state, whenever the user changes it. A bound value doesn't run it. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uitoggleswitch-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::ToggleSwitch>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

## `ui::ToggleSwitchControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::ToggleProvider`.

A boolean on/off switch: a pill-shaped track with a sliding thumb, an optional header above it and a label beside it that follows the state.

Use it for a setting that takes effect immediately (a [CheckBox](check-box.md#uicheckbox) is for a choice confirmed later). A click released over the control, or Space on key-up while focused, flips [checked()](#checked) and fires [on_checked_changed()](#on_checked_changed). The control reserves the width of the wider of its two labels, so flipping it never reflows its row. With animations running, the thumb slides and grows on hover. Otherwise it snaps.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> wifi{true};

auto  stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* sw    = stack->add(std::make_unique<ui::ToggleSwitchControl>(true));
sw->set_header("Wi-Fi");
sw->on_checked_changed([&](bool on) { wifi = on; });

// Or declaratively, kept in step with the Property:

    .header             = "Airplane mode",

    .checked_text       = "Flying",
    .unchecked_text     = "Grounded",
    .on_checked_changed = [&](bool on) { wifi = !on; },
```

### ToggleSwitchControl

```cpp
ToggleSwitchControl()
```

An enabled switch, off, with the "On"/"Off" labels and no header.

### ToggleSwitchControl

```cpp

```

A switch starting in `on`; the initial state never fires [on_checked_changed()](#on_checked_changed) or animates.

The label beside the track while on: the control's own, else [strings()](../core/namespace-ui.md#strings).toggle_switch.on ("On").

Replaces the on label, or with nullopt goes back to [strings()](../core/namespace-ui.md#strings).toggle_switch.on. Updates the layout, since the control is as wide as its wider label.

```cpp
void set_unchecked_text(std::optional<std::string> text)
```

Replaces the off label, or with nullopt goes back to [strings()](../core/namespace-ui.md#strings).toggle_switch.off. Updates the layout, as [set_checked_text()](#set_checked_text) does.

An icon shown beside the track while on, in place of [checked_text()](#checked_text). Unset (the default) shows the text; with an icon, [checked_text()](#checked_text) still names the state for UI Automation.


Sets the off icon, or clears it with an empty source. Updates the layout.

### checked

```cpp
bool checked() const
```

Whether the switch is on. Off by default.

### set_checked

```cpp
void set_checked(bool on)
```

Changes the state and redraws. Does nothing when unchanged. Otherwise fires [on_checked_changed()](#on_checked_changed), also when called from code.

### on_checked_changed

```cpp
void on_checked_changed(Callback<void(bool)> handler)
```

Invoked with the new state whenever [checked()](#checked) changes (click, Space, UI Automation or [set_checked()](#set_checked)). Replaces any previous handler.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Implement these instead of [measure()](../tree/element.md#measure) and [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange). The base class has already applied margin, size limits and alignment by the time these run. [measure_override()](#measure_override) is pure (every concrete [Element](../tree/element.md) must size itself); [arrange_override()](#arrange_override) defaults to a no-op since most leaves need nothing beyond having [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds) set, which the base already did.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Position children within the rect [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange) settled on (also in [bounds()](../tree/element.md#bounds), window DIPs). Default: nothing, for a leaf.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A pointer event for this element: the element under the pointer, one inside it that did not handle the event, or the element holding the capture. The position is in layout coordinates ([handle_pointer()](../tree/element.md#handle_pointer)). Return true when the event did something here, and it goes no further up; a handled press also captures the pointer until its release. A control that acts on a press (a click, a toggle, a caret placed, a drag started) returns true for the press and its release, so a list row or a card around it does not act on the same click. Default: false.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

What the control draws, in layout coordinates; [render()](../tree/element.md#render) has already applied the visual layer. A container draws its children through their [render()](../tree/element.md#render), never their [render_override()](#render_override).

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the knob's slide and resize.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Keyboard focus arrived (true) or left (false); [is_focused()](../tree/element.md#is_focused) already says so. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

A key for this element: the focused one, or one inside it that did not handle it. Return true when the key did something here, and it goes no further; false lets it bubble on to the parent and then to the shortcuts, a dialog's default button and arrow-key focus moves. Default: false.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme& theme) const override
```

Around switch and label, or the switch alone, as the theme places it.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme& theme) const override
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.
